newsitem.title: JAPAN: Copper mine output to rise five pct in 1997--IWCC.
newsitem.headline: Copper mine output to rise five pct in 1997--IWCC.

text.p: Copper mine production outside the CIS and China was expected to rise by five percent this year to almost 9.9 million tonnes, the International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC) said on Wednesday.
The IWCC also said in a statement that it expected mine output to climb a further seven percent in 1998.
Refined copper production last year rose by nine percent to 10.6 million tonnes and was seen rising by seven percent in 1997, the IWCC said.
Consumption grew by four percent last year and was expected to rise by around three percent this year and next to more than 11.5 million tonnes, it said.
The industry body estimated that the supply-demand balance for refined copper last year was at a slight surplus and said that the surplus would grow in 1997 and 1998.
The IWCC said, however, that these estimates were dependent on the outflow of copper from the CIS and imports by China.
The IWCC is holding its 53rd joint meeting with copper producing and marketing companies in Kobe, western Japan, this week.
